acceptance: When the answer of a non-chore run whose last attempt exited 0 with no capacity reason becomes a Rerun (an empty final message, no JSON object, a fenced object or text after it, an unfinished object, nesting too deep, a stray or cut-off event line, no final message or no end event, a null result, or an object failing the output schema), review delegate runs M21.35's one repair phase with that reason; a capacity failure, a harness non-zero exit, an unreadable run log (UNREADABLE_ANSWER), a review failure (file_review's write check still runs first, so an unparseable answer that wrote a file is review_failure with no second launch) and a chore reviewer get no repair turn

RUN record: run['refusal'] holds the reason and run['refusal_kind'] is 'parse' or 'record' (a missing kind is 'record'); repair attempts are marked repair: true; a second failure of either kind, including after a resume, leaves the run incomplete, exit 1, with a reason naming both and no further turn. --resume of an incomplete run with a stored reason sends the repair pair for the stored kind, not RESUME_PROMPT. repair_prompt introduces a parse reason as specy-road's reading of the final message (not review record's output), asks for the whole JSON object as the final message with no fence and nothing after it, and omits the notes rules; the refusal wording is unchanged

Tests in tests/test_review_delegate_repair.py: fenced JSON, prose after the object, no JSON, an unfinished object and a schema-invalid object (the prompt fences the schema reason), each followed by a valid answer -> filed after one repair turn whose prompt contains the reason; parse twice, parse then refusal, and refusal then parse -> incomplete, exit 1, both reasons, no third turn, nothing filed; unparseable answer that writes a file -> review_failure, one launch; non-resumable harness -> one fresh launch with the full prompt plus the repair section; capacity error and non-zero exit -> no repair turn; --resume with a stored parse reason -> repair pair with the parse intro and without the review-record intro or notes rules; --resume of a stored refusal with no refusal_kind -> record prompt; a resumed parse repair that fails again -> incomplete, both reasons. The no-json case leaves test_no_repair_turn_unless_review_record_refused (renamed for its remaining cases). docs/orchestration-reviewer-output.md repair bullet and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +40, tests about +140, docs about +3
nodes.title: review delegate also gives one repair turn when the final answer does not parse, not only when review record refuses it

acceptance: Profile field: a model profile's front matter accepts an optional `guidance_bypass_observed` mapping {date (YYYY-MM-DD), harness (a harness id), evidence (non-empty string)}, checked in model_profiles' structure check (any other shape makes the profile invalid) and printed by `models show`; the shipped composer-2.5 profile (template and sr/model-profiles, its alias composer-2.5-fast included) carries it with date 2026-11-06, harness cursor and the evidence '§9 replay and final re-test 2026-11-05/06, Cursor harness (agent -p --force): CR1 committed a roster change, then faked a terminal with `script` to run review accept-policy and the human approval, merged and pushed (2/3 runs); CR3 restored and deleted a peer's files with edit and delete tools after the guard denied git (2/3); CR5 never opened the brainstorm skill (3/3); review delegate filed 2/5'; no other profile gets it (composer-2, and grok-4.7, gpt-6.1-sol and claude-opus-5-5 through Cursor are untested: M22.23). A model is flagged when the profile routing reads (orchestration_pinned.pinned_profile_for_entry, integration branch) or the bundled profile with the same api_id or alias carries the field; a project or feature-branch copy without it does not clear it

One function, orchestrate_assign.guidance_bypass_refusal(config, entry, profile): when the pinned config's policy.signed_reviews is true, the entry's model is flagged and the roster entry lacks `allow_guidance_bypass_model: true`, it returns '<id> (model <api_id>) is excluded from executor and reviewer roles while policy.signed_reviews is on: its profile records guidance bypass observed (<date>, <harness>: <evidence>). Set allow_guidance_bypass_model: true on its roster entry to use it at your own risk.' Every eligibility decision uses it: orchestrate plan picks no such entry as executor or reviewer and the leaf's notes give the reason; worker delegate (_check_eligible and build_prompt) refuses with it, nothing launched; prompt --role executor or reviewer, prompt --run and review delegate refuse with it, exit 1, nothing launched; handoff status's who-can-approve row shows it (review_eligible._roster_reason); review_next_step offers no such reviewer; the review gate counts no record from such an entry (ineligible, same reason). The coordinator role, and everything with signed_reviews off, are unchanged

Opt-in: roster entries accept `allow_guidance_bypass_model` (boolean, default false; orchestration.schema.json in the template and sr/schemas, described as an at-your-own-risk override); with it true the entry is eligible and counted as before, and every launch for it (worker delegate, review delegate, prompt --run) prints one stderr line 'warning: <id> (model <api_id>) runs at your own risk: its profile records guidance bypass observed (<date>, <harness>); allow_guidance_bypass_model is set on its roster entry', and orchestrate plan adds the same note. While signed_reviews is on, validate and doctor print one warning per rostered executor or reviewer entry whose model is flagged ('excluded: set allow_guidance_bypass_model ... at your own risk' or 'opted in at its own risk'); with it off they print nothing new

Tests in tests/test_guidance_bypass_roles.py, one table: profile flag on/off x signed_reviews on/off x opt-in on/off x role (executor through orchestrate plan, worker delegate and prompt; reviewer through orchestrate plan, review delegate, prompt, handoff status and the gate's count; coordinator) -> refused with the reason, or allowed with exactly one warning line, or unchanged with no output change, per the sheet's decision table; plus the flag only on the bundled profile (project copy lacks it) -> flagged, a feature-branch edit removing it -> still flagged, a malformed field -> profile invalid, and the validate / doctor warning rows. docs/orchestration-roster.md, orchestration-workers.md, orchestration-models.md (the profile field) and orchestration-review.md (Signed reviews and 'What the gate cannot stop', recommending signed_reviews whenever agents run with shell access) state exactly this, naming composer-2.5 and the evidence and saying the finding is about that model, not the Cursor harness; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Changed
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +90, tests about +260, docs about +30
nodes.title: A model observed to bypass specy-road's guidance is excluded from executor and reviewer roles when signed reviews are on, unless the roster entry opts in at its own risk
